newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end firmer after late buying spree.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end firmer after late buying spree.

text.p: Australian shares closed firmer on Thursday after a late buying spree spruced up an otherwise lifeless session as investors contemplated the future direction of local interest rates.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 13.5 points higher at 2,350.2, well off its intra-session low of 2,329.3.
Brokers said low turnover indicated that investors remained squarely non-committal ahead of next week's Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) board meeting and the imminent U.S. elections.

"I couldn't pinpoint the cause of the late buying but I suspect that the weaker building approvals number this morning would not have been bad for sentiment," said Helen Michael, a dealer at Melbourne brokerage, Peake Lands Kirwin.
Michael said the bank sector was once again the focus of buying interest as investors continued to speculate about the likelihood of a near-term monetary easing.
Three out of four of the major banks were amongst the ten most active stocks on the day with ANZ, National Australia and Westpac shares all ending firmer and well off their lows.
Westpac was an outstanding performer, its shares closing 17 cents higher at A$7.20 (US$5.69) on turnover of 3.15 million shares.

Outside of the bank sector the market was relatively subdued. Chemical manufacturer ICI Australia provided some minor interest, slipping 20 cents to A$12.40 after Wednesday's 26.7 percent lower full year profit of A$197.1 million.
